---
title: "Tables"
guide-section: "Using tinytab"
---

A [`Table`](../reference/Table.qmd) holds data in columns, and renders it as text or HTML.

## Creating a table

Pass a dictionary that maps each column name to a list of values. All the columns must have the
same length:

```{python}
from tinytab import Table

menu = Table(
    {
        "item": ["coffee", "bagel", "croissant"],
        "price": [3.5, 2.25, 4.0],
        "sold": [120, 45, None],
    }
)

menu.columns, menu.n_rows
```

In a notebook, or on a page like this one, a table displays as HTML. Missing values (`None`)
show as empty cells:

```{python}
menu
```

## Formatting columns

[`Table.fmt()`](../reference/Table.fmt.qmd) attaches a formatting function to a column. Any
function that takes a value and returns a string works, including tinytab's own formatters:

```{python}
from tinytab import fmt_currency

menu.fmt("price", fmt_currency)
```

`fmt()` returns a *new* table and leaves the original unchanged, so calls can be chained, one
per column:

```{python}
from tinytab import fmt_number

menu.fmt("price", fmt_currency).fmt("sold", lambda x: fmt_number(x, decimals=0))
```

Formatters are never given missing values, so a formatter doesn't need to handle `None`.

## Rendering as text

[`Table.as_text()`](../reference/Table.as_text.qmd) renders a Markdown-style text table, ready to
print or paste into a Markdown document:

```{python}
print(menu.fmt("price", fmt_currency).as_text())
```

## Rendering as HTML

[`Table.as_html()`](../reference/Table.as_html.qmd) returns the HTML as a string, for use in a
web page or report:

```{python}
print(menu.fmt("price", fmt_currency).as_html())
```

Every value is HTML-escaped, so text in the data can never be mistaken for markup:

```{python}
Table({"name": ["<b>bold</b>", "Tom & Jerry"]})
```

## Saving and loading

[`Table.to_csv()`](../reference/Table.to_csv.qmd) writes the table's values to a CSV file, and
[`Table.from_csv()`](../reference/Table.from_csv.qmd) reads one back:

```{python}
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "menu.csv"
menu.to_csv(path)

Table.from_csv(path)
```

Two things to know about CSV files:

- Formatting isn't saved. `to_csv()` writes the original values, not the formatted ones.
- CSV files don't record types, so `from_csv()` reads every value as a string.
